Recruiters often have only a jobseeker's number or email address to hand.
Hence, each keyword is now matched, case-insensitively and as a substring,
against the name, phone number and email. The fields are checked separately
so a keyword cannot match across a field boundary (e.g. Alice12345).
Tags are still not searched.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix edge case bug caused by em-space
commitResults.messageBody:
Previously, having an em-space-only argument to findj/findc causes IllegalArgumentException to be
thrown from isBlank NameContainsKeywordsPredicate.java, instead of the expected ParseException.
This could have caused the app to show an uncaught exception since MainWindow.java only catches
CommandException or ParseException. The IllegalArgumentException goes past that handler,
so the user gets no “Invalid command format” message, just an uncaught exception.

However, in this commit, this has been fixed such that em-space-only argument would now correctly
cause ParseException to be thrown.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add hidden status to jobseekers and clients
commitResults.messageBody:
Previously, a recruiter can set aside a jobseeker or client only by
deleting them, which loses their details and notes, even when the
recruiter may want to work with them again later.

The planned hidej/hidec, unhidej/unhidec and hidden-list commands
solve this, but they all need each jobseeker and client to remember
whether it is hidden, across restarts.

Let's,
* give each jobseeker and client a hidden status, saved under a
  hidden key in the data file
* require the status in every Jobseeker and Client constructor, so
  code that creates or rebuilds a person must state it instead of
  getting a silent default
* make new and sample jobseekers/clients as unhidden by default
* keep the hidden status unchanged when editj, tagj, untagj, tagc and
  untagc rebuild the person they change

Hidden people stay in the existing jobseekers and clients lists of the
data file instead of moving to separate lists. Duplicate checks then
still cover hidden people, and hiding or unhiding becomes an in-place
update. A missing hidden key is read as unhidden, so existing data
files load without any migration.

No command reads or changes the status yet, so the app behaves as
before. The hide, unhide and list commands will follow in later
commits.

Previously, jobseekers and clients have a hidden status, but no view
uses it. listj, findj, listc and findc, the view at startup and the
view after editj all show hidden people alongside everyone else.

Hiding someone is meant to take them out of the recruiter's everyday
lists. Without that, the planned hidej and hidec commands would have
no visible effect.

Let's,
* make listj and listc show only unhidden people
* make findj and findc search only unhidden people
* show only unhidden people at startup and after editj

Hidden people are only left out of the view, not removed from the
address book, so they keep their details and can be listed or found
again by the planned commands for hidden people. The show-all
predicates are replaced rather than kept alongside, as no view shows
hidden and unhidden people together.

Tests that edit or tag a hidden person now show everyone first,
because they relied on hidden people appearing in the default view.

Previously, jobseekers and clients can be hidden, and listj, findj,
listc and findc leave hidden people out, but no command hides anyone.
A recruiter who wants someone out of their everyday lists can only
delete them, which loses their details and notes.

Let's,
* add hidej INDEX and hidec INDEX, which hide the jobseeker or client
  at that index in the displayed list
* report "no change" when hiding someone who is already hidden

Hidden jobseekers/clients are kept in the address book with all their
details, so that a later unhide command can bring them back.

The test helpers showJobseekerAtIndex and showClientAtIndex now leave
out hidden people, to match findj and findc, which they stand in for.
Add jobseekers/clients hide command

hidej and hidec take people out of the jobseeker and client lists, but
no command shows hidden people again. A recruiter cannot check who
they have hidden, and a later unhide command would have no list to
pick an index from.

Let's,
* add listhj, which lists only hidden jobseekers
* add listhc, which lists only hidden clients

Each command changes only its own list, as listj and listc do, so a
recruiter can look through hidden jobseekers while the client list
keeps showing what it showed before.

Commands to search through hidden people (findhj and findhc) will
follow in a later commit.

listhj and listhc show every hidden jobseeker or client, but findj and
findc search only unhidden people. A recruiter who has hidden many
people has to scroll through the whole hidden list to find one of
them.

Let's,
* add findhj, which searches only hidden jobseekers
* add findhc, which searches only hidden clients

Both commands take the same keywords and match them in the same way
as findj and findc, so recruiters need not learn a second search
syntax. Each command changes only its own list, as findj and findc do.

The result message says "hidden", e.g. "2 hidden jobseeker(s)
listed!", so that recruiters can tell which list they are looking at.

commitResults.messageTitle: Test listhj and listhc after findhj and findhc
commitResults.messageBody:
Previously, the tests for listhj and listhc start from the default
view, which shows no hidden people. They would still pass if either
command narrowed the list already on screen instead of replacing it,
for example by keeping only the hidden people that a previous findhj
search showed.

Let's add a test for each command that first runs findhj or findhc to
show one hidden person, then checks that listhj or listhc lists every
hidden person again.

Each test also checks that the search did narrow the list, so that it
cannot pass merely because the search happened to show everyone.

commitResults.messageTitle: Allow names to contain any character except '/'
commitResults.messageBody:
Previously, names were limited to letters, digits and spaces. Our
feature specification says that a name can be anything that does
not contain '/', so valid names were being rejected:
* company names with punctuation, e.g. Hershey's, McDonald's
* names with non-ASCII characters, e.g. X Æ A-Xii
* names with accented letters, e.g. Zoë Núñez

Change Name.VALIDATION_REGEX to "[^\\s/][^/]*":
* '/' is still banned anywhere in a name, because commands use it
  in field labels such as n/ and p/.
* The first character still cannot be a space, so a name made only
  of spaces is rejected and names still cannot be blank.
